title: Filter HTTP 500 Server Errors with Line Numbers
description: Examine 'httpd_access.log' in the scratch directory. Extract only the lines containing HTTP status code 500 (Internal Server Error) along with their line numbers.
objective: Output matching lines with line numbers from httpd_access.log
hints: Use grep -n to show line numbers.

title: Invert Match Comment & Empty Lines
description: Read 'sshd_config.test'. Filter out all comment lines (starting with '#') and all blank/empty lines to display active configuration directives.
objective: Display only active directives without comments or empty lines.
hints: Anchor comments with ^# and empty lines with ^$

setup_files.sshd_config.test:
# OpenSSH daemon configuration file
# Port 22
Port 2222

# Authentication:
PermitRootLogin no
# PermitEmptyPasswords no
PasswordAuthentication no

X11Forwarding no

title: Count Failed SSH Password Log Occurrences
description: Scan 'auth.log' and count the exact number of lines recording failed password login events.
hints: Use -c flag to count matching lines.

setup_files.auth.log:
Oct 07 10:14:02 rhel-node1 sshd[4912]: Accepted publickey for ansible from 10.0.0.5 port 51220 ssh2
Oct 07 10:15:18 rhel-node1 sshd[4980]: Failed password for root from 198.51.100.44 port 43120 ssh2
Oct 07 10:15:20 rhel-node1 sshd[4982]: Failed password for invalid user admin from 198.51.100.44 port 43122 ssh2
Oct 07 10:16:01 rhel-node1 systemd[1]: Started Session 48 of user root.
Oct 07 10:17:44 rhel-node1 sshd[5011]: Failed password for dbuser from 203.0.113.88 port 39810 ssh2

title: Match Exact Whole Word Using Boundary
description: Search 'services.txt' for lines containing the exact word 'root' (and NOT 'chroot' or 'rootfs').
hints: Use -w flag for exact word boundary.

setup_files.services.txt:
user: root process: bash
user: chroot_jail process: sftp
user: rootfs_audit process: daemon
user: root process: sshd

title: Display Lines with Context Surrounding Match
description: Search 'app.log' for lines containing 'FATAL' and display 2 lines before (-B 2) and 2 lines after (-A 2) each match.

setup_files.app.log:
INFO: Initializing database connection
DEBUG: Checking credentials
FATAL: Database connection pool exhausted
ERROR: Shutting down worker thread
INFO: Cleanup complete

title: List Only Filenames Containing Match
description: Search all '.conf' files in current directory for 'AllowOverride' and output only the filenames of matching files.
hints: Use -l flag to list files with matches

title: Match Valid IPv4 Address Lines with ERE
description: Search 'nodes.txt' for lines starting with an IPv4 address formatted as 4 numeric octets separated by dots.

title: SELinux Enforce Substitution
description: Modify 'selinux.conf' so that 'SELINUX=enforcing' is replaced with 'SELINUX=permissive'. Print modified output to stdout.

setup_files.selinux.conf:
# This file controls the state of SELinux on the system.
SELINUX=enforcing
SELINUXTYPE=targeted

title: Delete Comment Lines Using Pattern Addressing
description: Using sed, delete all lines beginning with '#' from 'crontab.test' and print the resulting scheduled tasks.
hints: Use pattern address delete: sed '/^#/d' crontab.test

setup_files.crontab.test:
# Daily backup crontab
# m h dom mon dow user command
0 2 * * * root /usr/local/bin/backup-db.sh
# Weekly audit
0 4 * * 0 root /usr/local/bin/security-audit.sh
# End of file

title: Replace Directory Path with Custom Delimiter
description: Replace '/var/www/html' with '/data/www/html' in 'vhost.conf' using custom delimiter '#' in sed.
hints: Use sed 's#find#replace#g' to avoid escaping slashes.

title: Print Specific Line Range with sed -n
description: Print lines 3 through 5 (inclusive) from 'audit.log' using sed quiet mode (-n) and the 'p' print command.

setup_files.audit.log:
line1
line2
line3
line4
line5
line6
line7

title: Strip Leading Whitespace Indentation
description: Using sed, remove all leading spaces and tabs from each line in 'code.txt' and output the clean text.

title: Extract System Users with Bash Shell
description: Examine 'passwd.sample'. Using awk with delimiter ':', print username ($1) and UID ($3) formatted as 'user:UID' for any account whose login shell ($7) is '/bin/bash'.

setup_files.passwd.sample:
root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash
bin:x:1:1:bin:/bin:/sbin/nologin
daemon:x:2:2:daemon:/sbin:/sbin/nologin
ansible:x:1001:1001:Ansible Automation:/home/ansible:/bin/bash
dbadmin:x:1002:1002:Database Admin:/home/dbadmin:/bin/bash
apache:x:48:48:Apache:/usr/share/httpd:/sbin/nologin

title: Sum Column Values of Log Transfer Bytes
description: Read 'transfers.tsv'. Using awk, calculate and print the total sum of the transferred byte sizes located in column 2.
hints: Output in the END block: END {print sum}

setup_files.transfers.tsv:
backup_rhel10.tar.gz	5000	OK
kernel_rpm.rpm	1200	OK
logs_archive.zip	3800	OK
database_dump.sql	10000	OK

title: Print Last Field of Variable Length Log Lines
description: Read 'commands.log'. Extract and print only the final word/argument of each line using the built-in $NF variable.

setup_files.commands.log:
user run command restart
admin exec script --force deploy
system alert warning critical

title: Filter Human Interactive Users with UID >= 1000
description: Examine 'passwd.sample'. Using awk with delimiter ':', print the username of any account with UID ($3) greater than or equal to 1000 and less than 65534.

title: Case-Insensitive Recursive Search Ignoring Binaries
description: Search directory './configs' recursively (-r), case-insensitively (-i), ignoring binary files (-I), for the string 'API_KEY'.

title: List Files NOT Matching Pattern with grep -L
description: Search all '.conf' files in current directory and print only the names of files that do NOT contain the directive 'PermitRootLogin'.

title: Delete All Empty Blank Lines with sed
description: Read 'notes.txt'. Delete all blank lines (lines with zero characters) using sed pattern addressing.

title: Strip Windows Carriage Returns
description: Remove trailing Windows/DOS carriage return characters (\r) from each line in 'windows.txt'.

title: Custom Output Field Separator with OFS
description: Read 'users.tsv' (tab-separated). Print column 1 and column 2 formatted with custom output field separator ' -> ' using awk.
hints: Set OFS in BEGIN block: BEGIN {OFS=" -> "}
